title: Set a stroller's brakes, nudging it till the pins drop
instruction: Set both rear brakes on the stroller so it cannot roll, then let go.
context: Why: Before a child goes in or out, a parent sets the stroller's rear brakes. Each lever drops a pin between the teeth of a ring on the wheel's hub; when the pin lands on a tooth the lever stops short, looks pressed and springs back up when let go. The maker's instruction (Joovy Caboose manual, Rear Wheel Brakes): push down on the brake lever on each rear wheel; the stroller may need slight forward or rearward movement to line up the teeth on the brake with each wheel brake cluster; then push the stroller back and forth to check. A recalled stroller (CPSC 2011, Britax B-Nimble) is the warning: its pedal clicked and stayed down with the wheels unlocked. A parent uses a foot; here a hand presses the lever lightly, nudges the stroller until the pin drops, then presses it home. Pressing alone, the natural move, leaves this brake unlocked. Done by: parents and carers, at every stop; here a two-arm robot at a bench.
setup: A real-size empty Joovy Caboose Too sit-and-stand stroller (aluminium frame, steel rear axle, plastic wheels with rubber treads; about 965 mm long, 515 mm wide, 1.07 m to the handlebar top, 12.5 kg), standing on a 1,300 x 900 x 12 mm plywood floor panel that runs from 200 mm in front of the robot past the table's far edge, its far end resting on a trestle level with the table top. Its rear is toward the robot, the rear axle 400 mm in front of the arm bases; front wheels (7 in, 178 mm) locked straight with their swivel locks. The two rear wheels (8 in, 203 mm) are 480 mm apart on one axle and turn independently; each has a ring of 12 brake teeth on its inner hub, tips 46 mm from the axle. Inboard of each rear wheel, a red brake lever pivots 50 mm above the axle: pushing its 40 x 30 mm pad down swings the lever through up to 25 deg and its pin toward the hub, into a gap between two teeth if one is there. A return spring pushes the pad up (6.4 N at rest, 20.4 N fully down, a light foot press within the arms' roughly 40 N; no published value, so measure the real stroller's with a spring scale before trials), and a detent catches the lever at 21 deg down and holds it there. Under each pad is the brake's housing on the axle bracket (part of the stroller's brake unit), so the pad can be pressed from above or pinched toward it. At the start both levers are up and each pin sits over a tooth tip, so a press alone stops well short of the detent and the lever springs back when let go. A substitute: any stroller whose rear brake drops a pin into hub teeth (the maker's manual: babiesgetaway.com/public/product_manuals/29.pdf). Layout fixed as in the screenshot.
scoring:
A brake is set when its lever is held down by its detent (caught at 21 deg; read as set from 19.5 deg down), which needs its pin between two teeth; then that wheel cannot turn (real trial: a 10 N push at the rear axle with a spring scale stops within 15 mm, the pin's play in its gap, and the wheel turns no further). Scores, highest level reached at the end:
- 0.0: no brake set, or at any time the stroller rolled more than 150 mm from its start or tipped more than 15 deg.
- 0.25: one brake set.
- 0.5: both brakes set.
- 0.75: both set and the stroller and levers still (moving less than 2 mm) over the last 2 s.
- 1.0: as 0.75, with no gripper within 30 mm of either lever's pad or pin or of the rear wheels over those 2 s.
Real trial: video of each lever and wheel, a tape measure for the roll, the spring-scale push for each set brake.
reset_notes: Lift both levers; roll the stroller until each pin sits over a tooth tip (marked on each hub) and set it on its floor marks with the front wheels locked straight; to put a pin over a tooth tip, lift that wheel 1 cm and turn it until the paint-marked tooth is under the pin.
fidelity: Rigid parts at real sizes; stroller body mass 12.5 kg. Wheels are hinges with light drag; brake lever (120 g, raised for the solver) is a hinge with a return spring (6.4-20.4 N at the pad: unpublished, so set as a light foot press; the demo also passes at half and double) and a detent rule holding it past 21 deg; the pin meets the tooth boxes (geometry, not a rule). Tooth count and lever geometry estimated from photos. A floor panel extends the table so the whole stroller stands.
